verdict.rationale: Amplitude Experiment's docs say you can ramp a flag-gated release, stage features for a percentage of users, and change flags remotely without a code change. They also mention a configurable bucketing unit (user, company ID, groups). However, nothing explicitly confirms deterministic or sticky bucketing across a ramp, or fine-grained 1%-to-100% percentage control. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of consistent/sticky bucketing as rollout percentage increases, documented percentage granularity and ramp mechanics, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can roll a flag out progressively by percentage with consistent bucketing, ramping from 1% to 100% without redeploying

citations.quote: Release behind a flag, ramp to the audience you choose, and turn it off the moment something looks wrong.
Pre-plan and stage new features for beta testers, a percentage of your users, or specific target audiences.
A payload is a JSON-coded set of variables that can remotely change flags and experiments without a manual code change.
In some B2B use cases, you might want to use company ID or city as the bucketing unit.
